name: Jürgen Habermas
summary: Jürgen Habermas, the Frankfurt School's second-generation theorist, defended deliberative democracy, constitutional patriotism and a deepened European Union, argued that capitalism must be tamed by a democratic state, and in his last years urged negotiations in the Ukraine war while holding that Ukraine must not lose.

sources.title: Moralischer Universalismus in Zeiten politischer Regression: Jürgen Habermas im Gespräch über die Gegenwart und sein Lebenswerk, Leviathan 48 (1/2020), pp. 7-28 (Internet Archive full text)
sources.author: Jürgen Habermas (interview, March 2019)
sources.usedFor: Interview on nation-state weakness against global markets, EU deepening, populism and religion in the public sphere (German original).

sources.title: ¿Necesita Europa una Constitución?, in La constitucionalización de Europa (Haberle, Habermas, Ferrajoli, Vitale; UNAM, 2004), Internet Archive full text (Spanish translation of his essay)
sources.author: Jürgen Habermas (essay, Spanish translation)
sources.usedFor: His proposals for a European constitution: Europe-wide referendums, social solidarity beyond the nation-state.

sources.title: Habermas für Verhandlungen zwischen Ukraine und Russland (epd report quoting his Süddeutsche Zeitung essay of 15 February 2023), evangelisch.de
sources.author: Jürgen Habermas (quoted in an epd report)
sources.usedFor: His call for timely negotiations while holding that Ukraine must not lose.

sources.title: Principles of solidarity. A statement (13 November 2023; Deitelhoff, Forst, Günther, Habermas), Normative Orders research centre, Goethe University Frankfurt
sources.author: Nicole Deitelhoff, Rainer Forst, Klaus Günther and Jürgen Habermas (joint statement)
sources.usedFor: The joint statement on Israel after 7 October 2023: Israel's counter-strike justified in principle, proportionality, rejection of genocide charge and of antisemitism, Israel's right to exist.

sources.title: February 15, or, What Binds Europeans Together: Plea for a Common Foreign Policy, Beginning in Core Europe (31 May 2003; with Jacques Derrida), excerpt in German History in Documents and Images
sources.author: Jürgen Habermas (text drafted by him, co-signed by Derrida)
sources.usedFor: The Iraq-war essay: a common European foreign policy beginning in core Europe, counterbalancing US unilateralism in the UN, effective transformation of international law and its institutions.

sources.title: War and Indignation (Süddeutsche Zeitung, 29 April 2022), English translation and excerpts on Thomas Gregersen's Habermas site
sources.author: Jürgen Habermas (excerpts)
sources.usedFor: On the West's dilemma between a Ukrainian defeat and escalation, arms deliveries and a negotiated compromise.

sources.title: Footnotes on Jürgen Habermas' lecture in Leuven about the European crisis (Protesilaos Stavrou, 2013), quoting the lecture 'Democracy, Solidarity and the European Crisis' (26 April 2013)
sources.author: Jürgen Habermas (quoted passages)
sources.usedFor: His Leuven lecture on the euro crisis: the steering capacities a monetary union needs must be centralised only in an equally supranational and democratic political community; warning against technocracy.

sources.title: Fundamentalism and Terror: a dialogue with Jürgen Habermas (Giovanna Borradori, Philosophy in a Time of Terror, University of Chicago Press, 2003; December 2001 interview), excerpt on the publisher's site
sources.author: Jürgen Habermas (interview)
sources.usedFor: His criticism of US unilateralism after September 11, the international criminal court and the case for cosmopolitan order and international police action.

sources.title: Jürgen Habermas, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, first published 2023
sources.author: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
sources.usedFor: Scholarly account of his constitutional patriotism, postnational constellation and politically constituted world society.

notFound.work: The 2013 Leuven lecture Democracy, Solidarity and the European Crisis (full text) and his 2011-12 Guardian euro-crisis articles

tried.how: both carry only a short introduction and links, not the lecture text

tried.how: the books exist only as borrow-only lending copies (access-restricted) so were not worked around; two unrestricted items (the Leviathan 2020 interview and a Spanish essay volume) were read
the 2022-23 Ukraine essays turned up only as press reports; the November 2023 'Grundsätze der Solidarität' text was not found

notes: First audit. Only open texts were available: a 2019 interview in Leviathan (German original) and his essay on a European constitution (Spanish translation, so medium at most), plus an epd report quoting his 2023 Süddeutsche Zeitung essay. The Ukraine essays (War and Indignation, 2022, read in English translation; the 2023 plea known from an epd report quoting it) hold that the West must avoid both a Ukrainian defeat and escalation to a nuclear war and match no statement cleanly, so were not scored. The 2013 Leuven lecture on the euro crisis was read through a commentary quoting it (the Social Europe text was unavailable) and his 2011 Guardian pieces were not found (see notFound). His secular-reason and religion remarks in the Leviathan interview (religion as a source of concepts of freedom and justice that secular reason must translate) were read and settle no statement. The December 2001 Borradori interview (publisher's excerpt) was read: its criticism of US unilateralism and support for an international criminal court are recorded. Most statements stay null; his lending-library books were not circumvented.
